entries.title: Hawaiʻi Climate Data Portal (HCDP) home
entries.summary: Front page of HCDP, the University of Hawaiʻi portal for quality-controlled climate data for Hawaiʻi and parts of the Pacific: near-real-time gridded rainfall and temperature maps, other climate variables, the Hawaiʻi Mesonet, climate summaries and storm reports. Its sections are Access Data, Hawaiʻi Mesonet, Climate Summary, Pacific Portal, Extreme Events and Climate Tools.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the portal's front page or an overview of everything HCDP offers.
example_queries: take me to the HCDP home page
what is the Hawaii Climate Data Portal
main page of the climate portal

entries.title: About HCDP (this site's About section)
entries.summary: This site's About section: what HCDP is, who builds it (UH Mānoa Water Resources Research Center, Hawaiʻi Data Science Institute / UH Information Technology Services, Sea Grant and partners) and how it is funded (NSF award OIA #2149133 and Hawaiʻi EPSCoR Change HI), with links to Team, History, Acknowledgements and How to Cite. Contact: hcdp@hawaii.edu.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks who runs HCDP, how it is funded, or wants the About pages in general.
example_queries: is HCDP part of the University of Hawaii

entries.title: Team
entries.summary: The people behind HCDP, the Hawaiʻi Mesonet and their cyberinfrastructure: HCDP Director Ryan Longman, Hawaiʻi Mesonet Director Thomas Giambelluca, cyberinfrastructure lead Sean Cleveland, plus researchers, software engineers, Mesonet technicians and contributors.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to know who works on HCDP or the Mesonet, or find a person's role.
example_queries: who is on the HCDP team
who built the climate data portal

entries.title: HCDP History
entries.summary: Why HCDP exists: Hawaiʻi's extreme climate gradients, scattered data sources, and how the portal grew out of the NSF EPSCoR ʻIke Wai project from 2018 (UH Mānoa Geography, Hawaiʻi Data Science Institute, WRRC and East-West Center) into a central source of near-real-time maps and data.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks how or why HCDP started, or wants background on climate data in Hawaiʻi.
example_queries: history of the climate data portal

entries.title: Rainfall Mapping History
entries.summary: How rainfall has been mapped in Hawaiʻi since the first gauge in Honolulu in 1837: early island maps, the Rainfall Atlas, the 1920–2012 month-year maps (Frazier et al. 2016), daily maps 1990–2014 (Longman et al. 2019), monthly maps 1990–2019 (Lucas et al. 2022) and HCDP's near-real-time mapping since 2022.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks how HCDP rainfall maps are made or about the history and methods of rainfall mapping in Hawaiʻi.
example_queries: how are the rainfall maps made
history of rainfall maps in Hawaii
who made the first rain map of Oahu

entries.title: Climate Monitoring History
entries.summary: The research station networks that preceded and feed HCDP: HaleNet on Haleakalā (since 1988), HavoNet in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Little HaleNet, HIPPNET, CraterNet, and the Hawaiʻi Mesonet.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about the history of weather stations and climate networks in Hawaiʻi.
example_queries: history of weather stations in Hawaii
old climate stations in Hawaii Volcanoes park

entries.title: Acknowledgements
entries.summary: Institutions, networks and people who contributed data, fieldwork and funding to HCDP, from UH units and federal agencies to ranches, parks, water utilities and citizen scientists.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to see who contributed to or supports HCDP.

entries.title: How to Cite
entries.summary: Citations for every HCDP product: the HCDP overview paper (Longman et al. 2024, Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society), the API and portal papers, and the method papers behind rainfall maps (1920–2012, 1990–2019, 2020–present), temperature maps, humidity, SPI, future projections and the four atlases.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor needs to cite HCDP data or maps in a paper, report or thesis.
example_queries: how do I cite the rainfall maps
what paper should I reference for the climate data portal

entries.title: Conditions of Use
entries.summary: HCDP's Conditions of Use page (first written for the Rainfall Atlas): images may be reproduced with the source credited; gridded and tabular data may be reproduced and distributed for non-commercial use with the source prominently stated; everything is provided without warranty. (Hawaiʻi Mesonet station downloads are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.)
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks whether the data is free, how it may be used or shared, or about licensing and commercial use.
example_queries: is this data free to use
can I use HCDP maps commercially
am I allowed to share the rainfall data

entries.title: Contact HCDP (hcdp@hawaii.edu)
entries.summary: HCDP's contact address is hcdp@hawaii.edu (questions, data requests, adding research to the library); Hawaiʻi Mesonet citation questions go to the same address.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to email or contact the HCDP team, report a problem or ask a question a page cannot answer.
example_queries: report a problem with the data
who do I ask about a missing station

entries.title: Access Data (interactive data portal)
entries.summary: HCDP's map viewer and download tool: gridded rainfall (1990 to yesterday, legacy monthly 1920–2012), mean/min/max temperature (1990 on), relative humidity (2002 on), NDVI (2000 on), fire ignition probability (2002 on), SPI drought index (1–60 months), 1991–2020 and 1978–2007 climatologies and downscaled future projections, statewide or by county, plus station values, time series and file export.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to explore or download HCDP maps or station data in the full portal tool, including datasets this site's viewer does not show (legacy rainfall, climatologies, projections).
example_queries: I need temperature maps for my research
where can I get GeoTIFFs of monthly rainfall

entries.title: Download maps and data files (GeoTIFF, CSV, zip)
entries.summary: In Access Data's export tab you pick a dataset, period and date range and tick the files you want: the data map GeoTIFF, standard-error map, anomaly map, anomaly standard error, metadata and error metrics, and station data (partial-filled or unfilled CSV); large requests are sent to your email.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants files: GeoTIFF grids, CSV station tables, bulk or multi-date downloads.
example_queries: get a csv of station rainfall

entries.title: Station data and station metadata
entries.summary: Access Data shows the rain gauges and temperature stations behind each map with their metadata (name, network, island, elevation, coordinates, IDs) and monthly or daily values as a time series; the station tables download as CSV, and the API serves the same through /stations.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants historical observations from a particular rain gauge or weather station, or the list and metadata of stations used in the maps.
example_queries: list of rainfall stations on Kauai
station metadata with elevation and coordinates
monthly rainfall at the Hilo airport station

entries.title: Legacy monthly rainfall maps, 1920–2012
entries.summary: Month-by-month rainfall maps for every month from January 1920 to December 2012 (Frazier et al. 2016), offered in Access Data as 'Legacy Rainfall'; this site's viewer covers the 1990-onward product only.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants rainfall maps from before 1990, long historical records or century-scale comparisons.
example_queries: monthly rain in the 1950s on Maui

entries.title: Climate normals (1991–2020 and 1978–2007 climatologies)
entries.summary: Average-climate maps in Access Data: contemporary 1991–2020 rainfall and mean/min/max temperature (monthly, wet and dry season, 30-year annual and decadal 1991–2000, 2001–2010, 2011–2020) and legacy Rainfall Atlas normals (1978–2007 annual; 1920–2012 monthly means).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants normal or average rainfall or temperature for a place or month, rather than a specific date.
example_queries: what is normal temperature in Waimea

entries.title: Future climate projections for Hawaiʻi (downscaled)
entries.summary: Downscaled rainfall and temperature projections in Access Data: statistical or dynamical downscaling, RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5, present day, mid-century (2040–2069) and late century (2070–2099 statistical, 2080–2099 dynamical), as projected values or change maps; rainfall also by wet and dry season.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about future rainfall or temperature, climate change scenarios or projections for Hawaiʻi.
example_queries: how much hotter will Maui get by 2100

entries.title: Fire ignition probability and 1–3 day predictions
entries.summary: HCDP's ignition probability is the daily chance of a large (8+ acre) wildfire ignition from current and past climate; Access Data also offers predicted ignition probability 1, 2 and 3 days ahead (the 3-day series starts 28 April 2025). This site's viewer shows the day-of map.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants fire risk for the coming days, a fire-weather outlook or the ignition-probability predictions.
example_queries: is fire risk high this week

entries.title: HCDP production files (public download URLs)
entries.summary: Every HCDP production file has a public, token-free download URL on ikeauth.its.hawaii.edu; this one is the statewide monthly rainfall GeoTIFF for August 2026, and other products follow the same …/HCDP/production/<datatype>/…/<extent>/<file type>/<year>/<file>.tif layout. The API's /files/production/list returns these URLs for a date range.
entries.when_to_use: A developer or GIS user wants a direct file URL pattern to script downloads without the portal.
example_queries: direct download link for the August 2026 rainfall GeoTIFF
URL pattern for HCDP tif files

entries.title: HCDP / Hawaiʻi Mesonet API (sign up for a token)
entries.summary: HCDP's programming interface for gridded maps, station data and Hawaiʻi Mesonet readings. This page has the sign-up form for an API token (required for most calls) and links to the documentation.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor writes code, wants bulk or automated access, or needs an API key/token.
example_queries: how do I get an API token
is there an API for the mesonet

entries.title: HCDP API documentation (endpoints and examples)
entries.summary: Swagger documentation for https://api.hcdp.ikewai.org with example curl calls: GET /raster (a GeoTIFF for datatype, period, date, extent), GET /raster/timeseries (values at one point over a date range), POST /genzip/* (zip packages), GET /files/production/list|retrieve, GET /stations, and the Mesonet endpoints. Calls send the token as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants endpoint details, parameters or example requests for the HCDP API.
example_queries: swagger docs for the climate data api

entries.title: API: gridded maps and point time series (/raster, /raster/timeseries)
entries.summary: GET https://api.hcdp.ikewai.org/raster?datatype=rainfall&production=new&period=month&date=2022-02&extent=bi returns a GeoTIFF; datatypes rainfall, temperature (aggregation min|max|mean), relative_humidity, ndvi_modis, ignition_probability, spi (timescale001–060); extents statewide, bi, mn, oa, ka. /raster/timeseries with lat and lng returns the values at one spot for a date range.
entries.when_to_use: A developer wants to fetch map grids or a time series at a coordinate by code.
example_queries: API call for monthly rainfall GeoTIFF
get rainfall time series at a lat lon with the api

entries.title: API: Hawaiʻi Mesonet measurements, stations and variables
entries.summary: GET https://api.hcdp.ikewai.org/mesonet/db/measurements?location=hawaii&station_ids=0145,0115&var_ids=RF_1_Tot300s&start_date=…&end_date=… returns 5-minute Mesonet readings; /mesonet/db/stations and /mesonet/db/variables list stations and variables; location=american_samoa serves the American Samoa stations; POST /mesonet/db/measurements/email mails large pulls.
entries.when_to_use: A developer wants live or historical Mesonet station readings by code.
example_queries: download mesonet station data with python
list all mesonet stations via api
api for american samoa weather stations

entries.title: API: bulk zip packages (/genzip)
entries.summary: POST https://api.hcdp.ikewai.org/genzip/email (or /genzip/instant/link, /instant/content, /instant/splitlink) with a list of datasets and a date range builds a zip of GeoTIFFs, metadata and station CSVs and emails a link (valid three days) or streams it.
entries.when_to_use: A developer or researcher wants many maps at once, e.g. every daily grid for a year.
example_queries: zip of all daily rainfall maps for 2025
email me a package of temperature grids

entries.title: HCDP API demo notebook (Python, GitHub)
entries.summary: A Jupyter notebook from the HCDP team showing how to use the API from Python: station metadata and values, gridded products, station and grid time series, and data packages sent by email. You need your own API token.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants example Python code for the HCDP API.
example_queries: python example for the HCDP API
jupyter notebook to download climate data
sample code to pull rainfall grids
how to use the api in python

entries.title: HCDP on GitHub (source code)
entries.summary: HCDP's GitHub organisation: the API server, the data portal viewer, the Guam and American Samoa viewers, the rainfall, temperature, humidity, NDVI, ignition and SPI production workflows, and Mesonet station metadata.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants HCDP's source code, workflows or technical repositories.
example_queries: github for the climate data portal
how are the maps produced code

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Mesonet station metadata (GitHub)
entries.summary: The source-of-truth repository for Mesonet station metadata: csv_data/stations/station_metadata.csv lists every station (ID, name, coordinates, elevation, SKN, NWS ID, status) for Hawaiʻi and American Samoa, with sensor positions and variable metadata alongside.
entries.when_to_use: A developer or researcher wants a machine-readable list of Mesonet stations and their metadata.
example_queries: station list with coordinates and elevation

entries.title: Tutorials
entries.summary: Step-by-step guides for the Access Data tool: make and download a map, explore station data and time series, and export data files. HCDP notes it is updating these tutorials; questions go to hcdp@hawaii.edu.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to learn how to use the data portal.
example_queries: how do I use the data portal
guide to the climate data portal

entries.title: Tutorial: make and download a map
entries.summary: How to navigate the map, choose a variable, time step and date, change the base layer, opacity and colour scheme, and download the map as a PNG in Access Data.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to make a map image or learn the map controls.
example_queries: how do I download a map image
change the color scheme on the map
save a rainfall map as png

entries.title: Tutorial: explore station data
entries.summary: How to select a station on the map or in the table, view its metadata, plot a time series (current month, year or all values) and download the chart in Access Data.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to see a station's data or time series in the portal.
example_queries: how to see data for one station
click a rain gauge and see its history

entries.title: Tutorial: export data
entries.summary: How to export files from Access Data: choose dataset, time period and date range, tick the files to include, and enter an email address (required for large requests).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to know how to download data files from the portal.
example_queries: why do I need an email to download

entries.title: Cultural Resources
entries.summary: Hawaiian and place-based climate knowledge: dryland agriculture, the Hawaiian moon calendar, indigenous drought perspectives, archival Hawaiian-language newspapers, a climate glossary, books, videos, courses and PDKE climate factsheets in English and Hawaiian.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor is interested in Hawaiian cultural knowledge of weather, climate, rain or drought, or teaching resources.

entries.title: Climate Glossary (Hawaiian weather terms)
entries.summary: Hawaiian words for sky, rain, rainbows, wind and other weather, e.g. ua (rain), ua lanipili (torrential rain), kualau (rain over the ocean), makani (wind), with their meanings.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks for Hawaiian names for rain, wind or weather, or the meaning of a Hawaiian weather word.

entries.title: Hawaiian Moon Calendar
entries.summary: The Hawaiian lunar calendar: moon phases, the twelve months, the Hoʻoilo (cool, wet) and Kauwela (hot, dry) seasons, and how moon phases guided traditional planting and fishing.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about the Hawaiian moon calendar, moon phases or traditional seasons.
example_queries: what moon phase is good for planting

entries.title: Indigenous Drought Perspective
entries.summary: How Kānaka Maoli experienced and responded to drought and what indigenous and local knowledge offers drought preparedness today, from a statewide survey, interviews and workshops.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor is interested in Native Hawaiian perspectives on drought.
example_queries: indigenous perspective on drought in Hawaii
how did Hawaiians deal with drought

entries.title: Dryland Agriculture
entries.summary: Rain-fed (unirrigated) Hawaiian field systems such as Puanui in leeward Kohala, with the Ulu Mau Puanui organisation and papers on their restoration.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about traditional rain-fed farming in Hawaiʻi.

entries.title: Hawaiian Newspapers (archival weather records)
entries.summary: How 1800s and 1900s Hawaiian-language newspapers record storms, floods and droughts (e.g. an 1871 hurricane), with links to the Kahua Aʻo project and the Ulukau newspaper collection.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants historical accounts of storms or weather from Hawaiian-language newspapers.

entries.title: Educational Resources
entries.summary: Books, web links, courses, videos, factsheets and publications about Hawaiian climate and resource stewardship, collected by HCDP.
entries.when_to_use: A teacher or learner wants reading lists, courses or learning materials about Hawaiʻi's climate.

entries.title: Climate Factsheets (PDKE)
entries.summary: Pacific Drought Knowledge Exchange factsheets in English and Hawaiian: 100-year drought history, future climate projections and El Niño impacts at Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and Puʻuwaʻawaʻa, fire history, and drought effects on conservation.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants short, printable summaries of drought, fire or climate change for a place or for managers.

entries.title: Library (publications)
entries.summary: HCDP's reference library of peer-reviewed articles and technical reports on Hawaiʻi's climate (400+), browsable and searchable (Publications Search page); authors can send missing PDFs to hcdp@hawaii.edu.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants scientific papers or reports about Hawaiʻi's climate, rainfall, drought or related research.
example_queries: find a paper on trade wind inversion

entries.title: Research Highlights
entries.summary: Short summaries of research using Hawaiʻi climate data: drought history, SPI, temperature trends, hourly rainfall, avian malaria, groundwater recharge, cloud water, station networks and more; researchers can submit their own.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants examples of research done with HCDP data or summaries of recent studies.
example_queries: what studies use the rainfall maps

entries.title: External Resources
entries.summary: Links to partner agencies and organisations: WRRC, Pacific Fire Exchange, USGS Pacific Islands Water Science Center, the State climate portal, PDKE, NWS Honolulu, PI-CASC, NCEI, RAWS, PacIOOS, UH Sea Level Center, watershed partnerships and county water departments.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor is looking for other climate, water or fire agencies and organisations in Hawaiʻi.

entries.title: Presentations (videos and webinars)
entries.summary: Recorded talks and webinars about HCDP: the portal launch, 'From soup to nuts' (PI-CASC), 'Unlocking Hawaiʻi's Climate Data' webinar, the climate data lifecycle, drought assessment, the Pacific Drought Knowledge Exchange, and new data tools for resource managers.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a video or talk introducing HCDP or its tools.
example_queries: video about the climate data portal
watch a talk on the Hawaii Mesonet

entries.title: Research: long-term gridded SPI for Hawaiʻi
entries.summary: Lucas et al. derived gridded monthly Standardized Precipitation Index maps at 250 m for timescales from 1 month upward, from 93 years (1920–2012) of monthly rainfall maps, and compared SPI-3 drought area with the U.S. Drought Monitor.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks how HCDP's SPI drought maps were developed or wants the SPI method paper.
example_queries: how is SPI calculated for Hawaii

entries.title: Research: a century of drought in Hawaiʻi
entries.summary: Frazier et al. synthesise a century of drought effects in Hawaiʻi using a 100-year (1920–2019) gridded SPI dataset, identifying major droughts from statewide SPI-12 and their meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, ecological and socioeconomic effects.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about the history of drought in Hawaiʻi or the worst droughts on record.

entries.title: Research: temperature trends 1917–2016
entries.summary: Mean air temperature in Hawaiʻi warmed about 0.05 °C per decade over 1917–2016 (Hawaiʻi Temperature Index), with signs of rapid warming at high elevations above the trade wind inversion.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks whether Hawaiʻi is getting warmer or about long-term temperature trends.

entries.title: Research: gridded hourly rainfall on Oʻahu (gauges + radar)
entries.summary: Huang et al. combined rain-gauge networks with weather radar to build gridded hourly rainfall for Oʻahu, with a published hourly gauge and radar dataset through 2020.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants hourly or sub-daily rainfall grids, radar rainfall or flash-flood research for Oʻahu.

entries.title: Research: drought effects on Maui drinking water
entries.summary: Surface water supplies about 27 percent of Maui's water, and most of upcountry and west Maui's; drought-reduced streamflow leads to frequent water-shortage declarations.
entries.when_to_use: A water utility, planner or resident asks how drought affects water supply, especially on Maui.

entries.title: UH Sea Level Center sea level forecasts
entries.summary: The UH Sea Level Center's outlook of monthly sea level anomalies one to two seasons ahead, combined with tide predictions for coastal water levels (HCDP itself does not produce sea level data).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about sea level outlooks, high tides or coastal water level forecasts.
example_queries: will sea level be high this winter

entries.title: Climate Tools
entries.summary: HCDP's list of decision tools: Rainfall Atlas, CCVD climate portfolios, H-RIP rangeland drought portal, Groundwater Recharge Tool, Monthly Climate Summary, State sea level rise viewer, American Samoa data viewer, SOEST coastal viewer, Climate of Hawaiʻi maps, and an avian malaria risk tool (coming soon).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a specialised tool rather than raw data, or asks what tools HCDP has.

entries.title: CCVD climate portfolios (Hawaiʻi Climate Portfolios)
entries.summary: Generates a climate and drought portfolio for any area in Hawaiʻi, from about 100 acres to a whole island: pick or draw an area, enter a name and email, and a PowerPoint of about 40 slides arrives by email.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a ready-made climate summary report for a specific property, ranch, watershed or area.
example_queries: make a climate portfolio for my farm

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Rangeland Information Portal (H-RIP)
entries.summary: Drought and rainfall conditions for ranches: pick an island and ranch to see rainfall, drought (NDMC), wind and the current ENSO (El Niño/La Niña) state; ranchers can submit new sites.
entries.when_to_use: A rancher or farmer wants drought or rainfall conditions for their pasture or ranch.
example_queries: ranch rainfall on the Big Island

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Groundwater Recharge Tool
entries.summary: Explores how changes in land cover and climate affect groundwater recharge, the main source of Hawaiʻi's fresh groundwater (built with the ʻIke Wai project).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about groundwater, aquifer recharge or how land use and climate change affect water supply.
example_queries: how does land cover affect groundwater

entries.title: State of Hawaiʻi Sea Level Rise Viewer (PacIOOS)
entries.summary: PacIOOS map viewer of potential sea level rise impacts in Hawaiʻi, listed on HCDP's Climate Tools page.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about sea level rise, coastal flooding or shoreline hazards in Hawaiʻi.
example_queries: which areas flood with 3 feet of sea level rise

entries.title: SOEST Coastal Viewer
entries.summary: UH SOEST viewer of coastal data for Hawaiʻi, listed on HCDP's Climate Tools page. The link did not respond when checked on 25 September 2026.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants coastal hazard or sea level data layers for Hawaiʻi.

entries.title: Avian Malaria-Risk & Warning (coming soon)
entries.summary: Listed on HCDP's Climate Tools page as coming soon and not yet available. A related research highlight describes a USGS-led tool combining HCDP daily temperature with mosquito development models to target mosquito control that protects native forest birds.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about avian malaria, mosquitoes or risk to native Hawaiian birds.
example_queries: where can mosquitoes spread malaria to birds

entries.title: Monthly Climate Summary
entries.summary: Hawaiʻi's monthly climate dashboard (beta): rainfall, temperature and drought for any month, statewide or by island, moku, ahupuaʻa, NOAA climate division or watershed, with anomalies, ranks against the record (rainfall back to 1920, temperature and drought to 1990), year-to-date percent of normal and history charts; email reports arrive around the 1st of each month.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to know how wet, dry, hot or cool a month was for an area, how it ranks, or to subscribe to monthly reports.
example_queries: was last month drier than normal

entries.title: Monthly Climate Summary how-to guide
entries.summary: How to use the Monthly Climate Summary: pick month and dataset, choose island and division (moku, ahupuaʻa, climate division, watershed), read anomaly, rank and year-to-date statistics, drought categories D0–D4 and W0–W4 from SPI-3, and subscribe to email reports.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants help reading or using the Monthly Climate Summary.
example_queries: how do I read the climate summary
what does rank mean in the monthly summary
how to subscribe to the climate report

entries.title: 2025 Hawaiʻi Annual Climate Report
entries.summary: Statewide summary of 2025: rainfall (42 in, the second driest year since 1920), drought (65% of the state abnormally dry), temperature (6th warmest in 35 years), monthly records, wettest, hottest and coolest days by island and place, and HCDP's 2025 highlights; a PDF is available.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a recap of last year's climate or 2025's records.

entries.title: 2025 Hawaiʻi Annual Climate Report (PDF)
entries.summary: The printable PDF version of the 2025 Hawaiʻi Annual Climate Report.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to download or print the annual climate report.

entries.title: Climate summary and event apps (full screen)
entries.summary: The web app behind the Monthly Climate Summary, the 2025 Annual Report and the storm pages, opened without the portal frame; its routes include #/nolo-viewer, #/lowell-tracker, #/lowell-focus, #/hurricane-lowell, #/hurricane-lala, #/storm-viewer (Kona low #1), #/storm-viewer-march2026-2 (Kona low #2) and #/climate-summary-2025.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the full-screen version of the monthly summary or an event tracker, e.g. on a phone.
example_queries: open the climate summary full screen
storm tracker without the website frame

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Mesonet
entries.summary: Hawaiʻi's statewide network of automated weather stations (about 80 active and 25 planned in September 2026, toward roughly 100): each records rainfall, air temperature, humidity, wind, pressure, radiation, soil temperature and soil moisture as 5-minute statistics and reports every 15 minutes; equipment was funded mainly by NSF with the State water commission and the Honolulu Board of Water Supply.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to learn about the Mesonet, what the stations measure, or current station readings.
example_queries: how many weather stations are there

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Mesonet Live Data Access
entries.summary: Live readings from every Hawaiʻi Mesonet station: map and table search, a dashboard per station (current rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity, solar radiation, soil moisture), graphs of up to three variables over 90 days, station climatology, data maps, a wind map, and downloadable station reports.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants current or recent conditions at a station: is it raining now, how windy, today's temperature.
example_queries: is it raining in Hilo right now
what is the temperature at the Lyon Arboretum station now

entries.title: Mesonet station list (table search)
entries.summary: Searchable table of Hawaiʻi Mesonet stations with ID, name, status, island, latitude, longitude and elevation; pick one to open its dashboard.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the list of Mesonet stations, one station's location, or stations on an island.

entries.title: Mesonet station map
entries.summary: Map of all Hawaiʻi Mesonet stations; click a station to open its live dashboard.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to find a Mesonet station on a map or the nearest station to a place.

entries.title: Mesonet data map (latest observations)
entries.summary: Map of the latest observation at every station for a chosen variable (air and soil temperature, 24-hour rainfall, solar radiation, humidity, soil moisture, wind) in metric or standard units.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a statewide snapshot of current conditions, e.g. rainfall in the last 24 hours at all stations.

entries.title: Mesonet wind map
entries.summary: Map of current wind at Hawaiʻi Mesonet stations.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants current wind speed and direction across the islands.
example_queries: how windy is it right now

entries.title: Mesonet station reports (download station data)
entries.summary: Generate a report of 34 variables for one Mesonet station over a date range, as a CSV export or emailed package (up to 5 reports per 15 minutes); data are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to download past Mesonet readings for a station as a file.
example_queries: export a station's data for last month
get 5 minute data for a station

entries.title: Mesonet graphs (up to three variables)
entries.summary: Plot up to three variables for a Mesonet station over the last days or a custom range of up to 90 days, in metric or standard units.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a quick chart of a station's recent readings.
example_queries: graph rainfall at a station this week
chart wind for the last 30 days

entries.title: Mesonet station climatology
entries.summary: Typical monthly climate at a Mesonet station's location, taken from HCDP's gridded 1991–2020 contemporary climatology (not from the station's own short record).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants normal conditions at a station's location to compare with live readings.
example_queries: typical temperature at a mesonet site

entries.title: Hawaii Mesonet mobile app (hawaiimesonet.app)
entries.summary: A phone-friendly, installable web app with real-time Hawaiʻi Mesonet readings: stations near you, a map with wind arrows and charts per station (a separate American Samoa edition exists).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants live station readings on a phone or a mobile app.

entries.title: Climate Data Stations (station QR code page)
entries.summary: Landing page for people who scanned the QR code on a climate station: what the stations are for and how their data feed HCDP.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor found a weather station in the field (e.g. scanned its sign) and wants to know what it is.
example_queries: I found a weather station on a trail
scanned the QR code on a rain gauge

entries.title: American Samoa Mesonet Live Data Access
entries.summary: Live readings from the American Samoa Mesonet (10 active sites: weather stations and stream gauges on Tutuila and Aunuʻu), with station dashboards and graphs.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants current weather or stream gauge readings in American Samoa.

entries.title: Pacific Portal
entries.summary: HCDP's gateway to Pacific Islands climate information: data portals, regional organisations, country and territory pages, and tools and resources, plus the American Samoa and Guam climate data portals.
entries.when_to_use: Anything about Pacific Islands beyond Hawaiʻi: American Samoa, Guam, Micronesia, Marshall Islands, Palau and others.

entries.title: Pacific Portal: Data
entries.summary: Regional data sources for the Pacific Islands: Pacific Climate Change Portal, Pacific Environment Portal (SPREP), the USFS PNW-FIA Pacific Islands database, the Pacific Regional Data Repository and NIWA.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants climate or environmental data for Pacific island countries outside Hawaiʻi.

entries.title: Pacific Portal: Regional Organizations
entries.summary: Pacific regional organisations such as SPREP, the Pacific Community (SPC), the Pacific Islands Forum, FFA, USP and PI-CASC.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor is looking for Pacific regional agencies or organisations.
example_queries: who works on climate in the Pacific

entries.title: Pacific Portal: country and territory pages (Palau, Marshall Islands, FSM, Fiji, Samoa and more)
entries.summary: Country and territory resource pages (under development) for Guam, Marshall Islands, FSM, Kiribati, Fiji, Tonga, Nauru, Palau, Northern Mariana Islands, Cook Islands, Tokelau, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, New Caledonia, Tuvalu, Samoa, American Samoa, Niue and French Polynesia.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants climate resources for a specific Pacific island country or territory.

entries.title: Pacific Portal: Tools & Resources
entries.summary: Regional documents, country-specific NGOs, video resources (NIWA Island Climate Updates) and the Pacific Marine National Monuments weather stations.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants Pacific regional documents, NGOs or climate outlook videos.

entries.title: Pacific Marine National Monuments weather stations
entries.summary: US Fish and Wildlife Service weather stations in the Papahānaumokuākea, Pacific Remote Islands and Rose Atoll marine national monuments, monitored in real time, and how their data support wildlife management (albatross heat stress, nest flooding, invasive plants).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about weather data from the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands or other remote Pacific monuments and atolls.
example_queries: weather stations in the marine monuments

entries.title: American Samoa Climate Data Portal
entries.summary: A partner portal of HCDP for American Samoa: geospatial, environmental and real-time monitoring and gridded data portals, top climate datasets, future climate projections, the CRAG coral reef library and other American Samoa data tools.
entries.when_to_use: Anything about climate data for American Samoa.

entries.title: American Samoa data viewer and download
entries.summary: Map viewer for American Samoa: gridded rainfall (1980–2024) with maps and point time series, PRISM climatologies and CHELSA downscaled projections, with downloads.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants rainfall maps, time series or downloads for American Samoa.

entries.title: American Samoa live and gridded climate data
entries.summary: American Samoa's real-time climate (5 weather sites) and streamflow (4 gauges) data via the NWS, Synoptic and the AS Mesonet viewer, gridded rainfall 1980–2024, historical station data since 2015, and ASPA water-use data by village.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants current, historical or water-use data for American Samoa.

entries.title: American Samoa historical climate data
entries.summary: Raw 15- and 5-minute records from UH–ASPA weather stations (since 2015) and stream gauges, gap-filled series, daily summaries, and links to NWS, RAWS and NOAA observatory data for American Samoa.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants past station records for American Samoa.

entries.title: American Samoa future climate projections
entries.summary: Downscaled future climate projections for American Samoa (CHELSA CMIP5/CMIP6 and Wang and Zhang 2016 dynamical downscaling), annual and wet/dry season maps, with an explainer on downscaling.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about future rainfall or temperature in American Samoa.

entries.title: American Samoa top climate datasets
entries.summary: Key reports, papers and datasets for American Samoa, e.g. sea level rise after the 2009 earthquake, 21st-century projections for Guam and American Samoa, groundwater recharge on Tutuila and the PIRCA report.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants key studies or datasets about American Samoa's climate.
example_queries: American Samoa sea level rise study

entries.title: CRAG (Coral Reef Advisory Group) Library
entries.summary: Literature on coral reefs in American Samoa, collected in the American Samoa Climate Data Portal.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants coral reef research or reports for American Samoa.

entries.title: Guam Data Viewer (portal page)
entries.summary: HCDP's page for the Guam Climate Data Portal viewer: rainfall maps (1980–2024, including monthly), PRISM mean rainfall and min/max temperature climatologies, and CHELSA downscaled rainfall and temperature projections.
entries.when_to_use: Anything about climate data for Guam.

entries.title: Guam Climate Data Portal (viewer, full screen)
entries.summary: The Guam Climate Data Portal map viewer itself: rainfall 1980–2024, PRISM climatologies and CHELSA projections, with downloads (rainfall flagged experimental).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the Guam viewer directly, full screen.

entries.title: Rainfall Atlas of Hawaiʻi
entries.summary: Mean monthly and annual rainfall maps for the 1978–2007 base period with uncertainty, an interactive map with station data, month-year maps 1920–2012, rainfall trend maps, and downloads (GIS grids, isohyets, images, station data).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants long-term average rainfall for a place, isohyets, or the classic Rainfall Atlas.
example_queries: how much rain does Hanalei get in a year

entries.title: Rainfall Atlas interactive map
entries.summary: Click anywhere to get the mean annual rainfall and a graph and table of mean monthly rainfall (1978–2007), with uncertainty and station layers.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the average rainfall at a specific spot or address.
example_queries: average monthly rainfall at my house
rainfall at a point on the map
how rainy is Kula on average

entries.title: Rainfall Atlas downloads
entries.summary: Rainfall Atlas files: map images and isohyets (inches or mm), GIS grids (ESRI and ASCII, 250 m), Google Earth files, rain-gauge tables through 2012, the report, month-year maps 1920–2012 and trend maps; all mean maps use the 1978–2007 base period. (The portal's old Rainfall Atlas page now redirects to this site.)
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants Rainfall Atlas GIS files, images or shapefiles.

entries.title: Evapotranspiration of Hawaiʻi
entries.summary: Downloads from the Evapotranspiration of Hawaiʻi atlas: mean annual maps and GIS grids of actual and potential evapotranspiration (Penman-Monteith, Priestley-Taylor, grass reference), latent heat and related variables, plus the project report.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about evapotranspiration, evaporation, water loss or irrigation demand.
example_queries: how much water evaporates on Maui

entries.title: Solar Radiation of Hawaiʻi
entries.summary: Downloads from the Solar Radiation of Hawaiʻi atlas: mean annual maps and GIS grids of solar, clear-sky, diffuse, longwave and net radiation plus air temperature, wind speed, humidity and vapour pressure.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about sunshine, solar radiation or solar energy potential.

entries.title: Climate of Hawaiʻi
entries.summary: Downloads of mean annual climate maps: air temperature, wind speed, relative humidity, vapour pressure deficit, albedo, cloud frequency, soil moisture, canopy wetness, vegetation cover, leaf area index, land cover and more.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants average maps of climate variables other than rainfall (wind, humidity, clouds, soil moisture).

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Climate Atlases (status notice)
entries.summary: Notice that the original Rainfall, Evapotranspiration, Solar Radiation and Climate atlas websites were taken down for updating, with their data downloadable from HCDP's atlas pages; the Rainfall Atlas is back online at rainfall.geography.hawaii.edu.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor cannot find an old atlas website or asks where the atlases went.
example_queries: where did the evapotranspiration atlas go

entries.title: Extreme Events
entries.summary: Index of HCDP storm reports: Hurricane Lowell (September 2026), Hurricane Lala (August 2026) and the two March 2026 Kona low storms; the Tropical Storm Nolo tracker (from 22 September 2026) has its own page.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants storm reports or asks about recent extreme weather events.

entries.title: Tropical Storm Nolo Mesonet Viewer (live tracker)
entries.summary: Live tracker for Tropical Storm Nolo (from 22 September 2026, 10 pm HST): every active Hawaiʻi Mesonet station on a county-filterable map of rainfall totals or maximum gusts, a 5-minute replay, and per-station rain and wind charts, updated every 15 minutes. No HCDP storm report yet.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about Nolo: current rainfall, wind or gusts during the storm, or station observations.
example_queries: how much rain from Tropical Storm Nolo so far
Nolo wind gusts on the Big Island

entries.title: Tropical Storm Nolo tracker (full screen)
entries.summary: The same Nolo Mesonet tracker without the portal frame, better on phones.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the Nolo tracker full screen or on mobile.

entries.title: Hurricane Lowell report
entries.summary: HCDP's story of Hurricane Lowell, 6–8 September 2026, when the Category 2 storm passed close to Kauaʻi and Niʻihau: hourly 250 m wind maps for Kauaʻi and Oʻahu, daily rainfall maps (Waiʻaleʻale about 36 in over three days, Lower Limahuli over 17 in), storm-surf impacts and a 15-minute gust and rain animation.
entries.when_to_use: Anything about Hurricane Lowell: its rainfall, winds, damage or data.
example_queries: download rainfall data from Hurricane Lowell
how strong were Lowell's winds on Kauai

entries.title: Hurricane Lowell Mesonet Viewer
entries.summary: Station tracker for Hurricane Lowell from 7 September 2026, 12 am HST: rainfall accumulation, maximum wind and gusts at every reporting Mesonet station, with county filter and per-station charts.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants station-by-station rainfall or wind observations during Hurricane Lowell.

entries.title: Hurricane Lowell – Kauaʻi and Oʻahu Focus
entries.summary: 'Station Watch' for Hurricane Lowell: accumulated rainfall or wind and gusts at every reporting Mesonet station on Kauaʻi or Oʻahu, side by side on a shared scale, with numbered map pins.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to compare all stations on Kauaʻi or Oʻahu during Lowell.
example_queries: all stations side by side Lowell

entries.title: Hurricane Lala report
entries.summary: HCDP's report on Hurricane Lala, 14–16 August 2026, which skirted the south side of Hawaiʻi Island as a Category 1 hurricane with statewide flooding: daily and cumulative rainfall and wind maps by county, station charts, hour-by-hour wind maps, the wettest hour (radar, 15 August on Hawaiʻi Island) and a comparison with the NWS forecast; totals exceeded 45 in in spots.
entries.when_to_use: Anything about Hurricane Lala: its rainfall, winds, flooding or data.
example_queries: how much rain did Lala drop on the Big Island

entries.title: Kona Low storm #1 viewer (10–16 March 2026)
entries.summary: Storm viewer for the first March 2026 Kona low: daily and cumulative rainfall maps by county with min/average/max, Mesonet station charts, and highlights: Maui hit hardest (up to 62 in locally; 33.2 in in 24 h at Haleakalā Summit, 36.4 in at Kuiki) and winds often above 100 mph at Puʻuwaʻawaʻa on Hawaiʻi Island on 14 March.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about the first March 2026 Kona storm, Haleakalā's record rain or the Puʻuwaʻawaʻa winds.

entries.title: Kona Low storm #2 viewer (17–23 March 2026)
entries.summary: Storm viewer for the second March 2026 Kona storm, whose downpours on saturated ground caused severe flooding: daily and cumulative rainfall by county, 14-day totals for both storms (10–23 March), and the 23 March Mānoa and Pālolo 'rain bomb' flash floods (2–4 in per hour; 3.5–6.5 in at six Mesonet stations).
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about the second March 2026 Kona storm, the Mānoa/Pālolo flash floods or the two-storm totals.
example_queries: total rain from both March storms

entries.title: March 2026 Kona low storms (both events)
entries.summary: Two back-to-back Kona low storms, 10–16 and 17–23 March 2026, caused historic flooding statewide (UH reported more than 2 trillion gallons of rain in March); each has its own HCDP storm viewer.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about the March 2026 floods or storms without naming which one.
example_queries: how much rain fell in March 2026

entries.title: Hurricane Lane (2018): Fire and Rain
entries.summary: Research highlight on Hurricane Lane, 22–25 August 2018: Hawaiʻi Island averaged 17 in of rain and one site 57 in, the wettest tropical cyclone on record in the state, while wind-driven wildfires burned nearly 3,000 acres on Maui and Oʻahu.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor asks about Hurricane Lane or historic hurricane rainfall in Hawaiʻi.

entries.title: Hurricane Lowell rainfall map (7 Sept 2026, Kauaʻi)
entries.summary: Daily rainfall on Kauaʻi on 7 September 2026, the day Lowell passed closest (Waiʻaleʻale just over 23 in); change the date to 2026-09-06 or 2026-09-08 for the other storm days, or the extent to statewide or oahu. Add ?scale=extreme for the 0–250 mm scale.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to see a map of Hurricane Lowell's rain.
example_queries: show me the rain map from Hurricane Lowell

entries.title: Hurricane Lala rainfall map (15 Aug 2026, Hawaiʻi Island)
entries.summary: Daily rainfall on Hawaiʻi Island on 15 August 2026, the day of Lala's wettest hour there; the storm window is 14–16 August, and extent statewide shows all islands.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants to see a map of Hurricane Lala's rain.
example_queries: show Lala rainfall on the Big Island

entries.title: March 2026 monthly rainfall map (Kona lows)
entries.summary: Statewide rainfall for March 2026, the month of the two Kona low storms; switch the extent to maui or oahu, or use daily maps (e.g. /viewer/rainfall/day/2026-03-14/maui) for single storm days.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a map of the March 2026 storms' rainfall.
example_queries: how much rain fell in March 2026 map

entries.title: Daily rainfall map (viewer)
entries.summary: HCDP's gridded daily rainfall (250 m) for any day from 1 January 1990 to yesterday, statewide or by island; each day appears about a day later (API range on 24 Sept 2026: 1990-01-01 to 2026-09-23). Add ?units=in for inches, ?stations=1 for rain gauges, ?scale=extreme for the 0–250 mm storm scale, ?compare=YYYY-MM-DD for a second date.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants to see where it rained on a specific day: yesterday, during a storm, or on a date they remember.
example_queries: how much did it rain on Kauai yesterday
rainfall map for October 21 2025 on the Big Island
daily rain map Oahu last Tuesday
show me rain on Maui on Sept 7

entries.title: Monthly rainfall map (viewer)
entries.summary: HCDP's gridded monthly rainfall totals (250 m) from January 1990 to the last complete month, each published around the 1st of the next (API range on 24 Sept 2026: 1990-01 to 2026-08); legacy maps before 1990 are in Access Data. Add ?units=in for inches, ?stations=1 for rain gauges, ?compare=YYYY-MM for a second month.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants total rainfall for a month on a map, or to see two months side by side.
example_queries: how wet was March on Maui
compare rainfall this August with last August

entries.title: Mean temperature map (viewer)
entries.summary: HCDP's gridded mean air temperature, monthly from January 1990 to the last complete month, and daily from 1 January 1990 to yesterday at /viewer/temperature-mean/day/YYYY-MM-DD/{extent} (API range on 24 Sept 2026). Add ?units=f for Fahrenheit, ?stations=1 for stations, ?compare= for a second date.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants average temperature for a month or day on a map.
example_queries: how warm was it on Oahu last month

entries.title: Maximum temperature map: daytime highs, hottest places (viewer)
entries.summary: HCDP's gridded maximum (daytime high) air temperature, monthly from January 1990 to the last complete month, and daily from 1 January 1990 to yesterday at /viewer/temperature-max/day/YYYY-MM-DD/{extent} (API range on 24 Sept 2026). Add ?units=f for Fahrenheit, ?stations=1 for stations, ?compare= for a second date.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants daytime highs or heat on a map: the hottest places, a heat wave, a hot month.
example_queries: hottest places in Hawaii last month

entries.title: Minimum temperature map: overnight lows, coldest places (viewer)
entries.summary: HCDP's gridded minimum (overnight low) air temperature, monthly from January 1990 to the last complete month, and daily from 1 January 1990 to yesterday at /viewer/temperature-min/day/YYYY-MM-DD/{extent} (API range on 24 Sept 2026). Add ?units=f for Fahrenheit, ?stations=1 for stations, ?compare= for a second date.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants overnight lows or cold on a map: the coldest places, a cold night, frost on the mountains.
example_queries: how cold did it get upcountry

entries.title: Relative humidity map (viewer, daily)
entries.summary: HCDP's gridded daily relative humidity (%) from 1 January 2002 to yesterday, statewide or by island (API range on 24 Sept 2026: 2002-01-01 to 2026-09-23). There are no monthly humidity maps; ?compare=YYYY-MM-DD adds a second date.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants humidity or muggy or dry air for a day on a map.
example_queries: how humid was Honolulu on July 4

entries.title: Vegetation greenness (NDVI) map (viewer, daily)
entries.summary: HCDP's MODIS-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, a measure of vegetation greenness and plant health, from 10 March 2000, statewide or by island. It runs a few days behind the other daily maps (through 2026-09-20 on 24 Sept 2026).
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants vegetation greenness, plant health or drought stress on vegetation on a map.
example_queries: how green is the Big Island

entries.title: Fire ignition probability map (viewer, daily)
entries.summary: HCDP's daily probability (0 to 1) of a large, 8+ acre wildfire ignition given current and past climate, from 1 January 2002 to yesterday, statewide or by island (API range on 24 Sept 2026). Predictions 1–3 days ahead are in Access Data.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants wildfire risk or fire danger for a day on a map.

entries.title: Drought index SPI-1 map (viewer)
entries.summary: Standardized Precipitation Index for the past 1 month: below 0 is drier than normal (below −1 is drought), above 0 wetter; monthly from about 1990 (SPI-3 starts March 1990) to the last complete month. HCDP publishes SPI statewide only, so keep extent statewide (zoom with ?lat=&lng=&z=); Access Data also has 36-, 48- and 60-month SPI.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants a drought map for very short-term dryness or wetness: last month's rainfall against the record.

entries.title: Drought index SPI-3 map (viewer)
entries.summary: Standardized Precipitation Index for the past 3 months: below 0 is drier than normal (below −1 is drought), above 0 wetter; monthly from March 1990 to the last complete month. HCDP publishes SPI statewide only, so keep extent statewide (zoom with ?lat=&lng=&z=); Access Data also has 36-, 48- and 60-month SPI.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants a drought map for short-term (seasonal) drought; the Monthly Climate Summary's D0–D4 drought categories come from SPI-3.

entries.title: Drought index SPI-6 map (viewer)
entries.summary: Standardized Precipitation Index for the past 6 months: below 0 is drier than normal (below −1 is drought), above 0 wetter; monthly from about 1990 (SPI-3 starts March 1990) to the last complete month. HCDP publishes SPI statewide only, so keep extent statewide (zoom with ?lat=&lng=&z=); Access Data also has 36-, 48- and 60-month SPI.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants a drought map for medium-term drought over a season or two.
example_queries: drought over the last six months

entries.title: Drought index SPI-9 map (viewer)
entries.summary: Standardized Precipitation Index for the past 9 months: below 0 is drier than normal (below −1 is drought), above 0 wetter; monthly from about 1990 (SPI-3 starts March 1990) to the last complete month. HCDP publishes SPI statewide only, so keep extent statewide (zoom with ?lat=&lng=&z=); Access Data also has 36-, 48- and 60-month SPI.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants a drought map for medium- to long-term drought.

entries.title: Drought index SPI-12 map (viewer)
entries.summary: Standardized Precipitation Index for the past 12 months: below 0 is drier than normal (below −1 is drought), above 0 wetter; monthly from about 1990 (SPI-3 starts March 1990) to the last complete month. HCDP publishes SPI statewide only, so keep extent statewide (zoom with ?lat=&lng=&z=); Access Data also has 36-, 48- and 60-month SPI.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants a drought map for long-term drought that affects streams, reservoirs and groundwater.
example_queries: has it been a dry year

entries.title: Drought index SPI-24 map (viewer)
entries.summary: Standardized Precipitation Index for the past 24 months: below 0 is drier than normal (below −1 is drought), above 0 wetter; monthly from about 1990 (SPI-3 starts March 1990) to the last complete month. HCDP publishes SPI statewide only, so keep extent statewide (zoom with ?lat=&lng=&z=); Access Data also has 36-, 48- and 60-month SPI.
entries.when_to_use: Someone wants a drought map for multi-year drought.

entries.title: HCDP AI interface (data analysis assistant)
entries.summary: The separate HCDP analysis assistant: it queries HCDP gridded maps and Mesonet data to compute totals, averages, rankings, comparisons and trends and draws charts and maps; sign-in uses an access code.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants numbers, comparisons, computation or charts — analysis rather than navigation (e.g. total rain at a station, which station was wettest, a trend since 1990).
example_queries: how much rain fell in Hilo during Lowell
which station recorded the most rain yesterday
compare August rainfall on Maui and Oahu

entries.title: National Weather Service Honolulu (forecasts and warnings)
entries.summary: HCDP publishes observations and maps of what already happened, not weather forecasts; the NWS Honolulu office issues Hawaiʻi's official forecasts, watches and warnings (flash floods, high wind, surf), and its Central Pacific Hurricane Center issues hurricane advisories.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants a weather forecast, a warning or storm advisories, which HCDP does not provide.
example_queries: will it rain this weekend in Kona

entries.title: UH News: March 2026 floods, 2 trillion gallons
entries.summary: University of Hawaiʻi News story on the March 2026 storms: Hawaiʻi Mesonet and HCDP data showed more than 2 trillion gallons of rain statewide in March and historic flooding.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor (often a journalist) wants the press story or headline figures on the March 2026 floods.
example_queries: news story about the March floods

entries.title: UH News: Hurricane Lala, 1.3 trillion gallons
entries.summary: University of Hawaiʻi News story: Hurricane Lala dropped about 1.3 trillion gallons of rain on Hawaiʻi, 14–16 August 2026 (about 1.9 million Olympic pools), from HCDP's rainfall maps.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the press story or headline figures on Hurricane Lala.
example_queries: how many gallons did Lala drop

entries.title: UH News: Hurricane Lowell winds and rain on Kauaʻi and Niʻihau
entries.summary: University of Hawaiʻi News story: Hurricane Lowell brought 100+ mph winds and heavy rain to Kauaʻi and Niʻihau; Mount Waiʻaleʻale had over 23 in on 7 September and nearly 36 in over three days.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants the press story or headline figures on Hurricane Lowell.
example_queries: how much rain at Waialeale during Lowell

entries.title: UH News: the Hawaiʻi Mesonet project
entries.summary: University of Hawaiʻi News story introducing the Hawaiʻi Mesonet, the statewide weather and climate monitoring network, linked from the portal's Mesonet page.
entries.when_to_use: The visitor wants background or press coverage on why the Mesonet was built.

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Mesonet live dashboard for one station
entries.summary: The live Mesonet viewer opened on one station's dashboard (current readings, updated every 15 minutes). Use the station id from the station list; view=graphing shows charts for the station.
entries.when_to_use: Current conditions or live readings at a named place or station.
example_queries: is it raining in Hilo right now

entries.title: Hawaiʻi Mesonet graphs for one station
entries.summary: Time-series charts of a station's recent readings in the live Mesonet viewer.
entries.when_to_use: Recent trend or chart at one station without analysis.
example_queries: chart the last week at the Waimea station
show me a chart of temperature at Nahuku

entries.title: Monthly Climate Summary for one month
entries.summary: The monthly summary app opened on a chosen month (year and month number).
entries.when_to_use: How wet or warm a particular month was, statewide or by island, as a report rather than a map.
example_queries: how was August 2026 across the islands

entries.title: A shareable question link
entries.summary: A link to this site that asks the assistant a question on arrival — the way to share a question rather than a page.
entries.when_to_use: Only when the visitor asks how to share a question with someone else.
example_queries: how do I share this question
give me a link that asks this
can I send someone this question
